thread:
Maya: quick follow-up from the kernel-selection RFC — spotted a gap around how we bind memory affinity when switching between grouped-query and multi-query paths
Sam: yep, saw that too. main concern is KV cache placement + prefetch semantics
Liam: can you summarize the concrete failure mode?
Maya: sure — when the selector opts into grouped-query for latency, we sometimes keep per-batch KV on a different allocator than the per-request cache expects. results in extra memcpy on hot path
Olga: Oof. Is this the case where sequence-length variance triggers fallback to MQA and we rebind buffers?
Maya: exactly. short seqs -> GQ; some long ones in same batch -> MQA fallback. allocator id flips mid-invocation
Sam: two options: keep a unified allocator for KV (safer, potential memory overhead) or add a cheap aliasing layer that maps across allocators at runtime
Liam: aliasing layer sounds flexible but adds indirection per KV lookup. do we have perf numbers?
Maya: rough probe: aliasing adds ~0.6-1.2us per KV lookup on A100 under our microbench. unified allocator removes that but increases resident set by ~8% in worst case
Olga: 8% mem vs 1us latency — which is worse depends on SLO. customers on Dedicated might prefer predictable latency
Sam: also think about eviction/GC semantics. unified allocator simplifies GC boundary (single heap) whereas aliasing needs cross-heap pin/unpin protocol
Liam: can we adopt hybrid: unified small hot-KV pool + fallback aliasing for cold KV? keeps hot path fast and caps memory cost
Maya: I like that. For hot-KV we can keep it on the per-device pinned pool. cold ones allocated lazily on per-path heap and mapped via the alias table
Olga: how do we mark "hot"? frequency-based counters? TTL?
Sam: frequency counters with decay. cheap LFU sketch would work. maintain per-shard counters during runtime, promote when above threshold
Liam: sketch adds memory but tiny. need to ensure thread-safety across worker threads
Maya: we'll use per-worker counters and periodic merge to avoid sync on hot path
Olga: next: API/iface change. The kernel selector currently returns a variant enum. we need it to also return an "affinity hint" and an optional allocator preference string
Sam: add to selector contract: (variant, affinity_hint, allocator_hint?). keep allocator_hint optional so older selectors still valid
Liam: sounds good. add explicit contract doc and defaulting rules: if no allocator_hint, runtime picks unified hot pool or falls back to path heap based on selector.policy
Maya: I'll draft a small follow-up RFC describing the hot-KV pool, alias table proto, and selector contract. includes microbench results and mem tradeoffs
Olga: also include migration plan: we should ship aliasing first (low-risk), enable hybrid opt-in for Dedicated customers, then flip default after 2 weeks of telemetry
Sam: +1. add a small Canary that targets low-latency routes only
deploy-bot: deployment scheduled: test-canary/hot-kv-aliasing -> will roll 5% of traffic on staging cluster at 2026-04-02T03:00Z
Maya: thanks. I'll post the RFC draft in #eng-runtime later today and tag reviewers @Sam @Liam @Olga
Sam: great. lemme know if you want perf scripts or memory traces
Maya: will do. thanks all :rocket:
